name: AccuWeather

summary.text: AccuWeather, Inc. is a privately held commercial weather forecasting company whose origins trace to November 15, 1962, when Penn State graduate student Joel N. Myers began forecasting winter weather for the Pennsylvania utility Columbia Gas; it is based near State College, Pennsylvania. Federal lobbying disclosures list it as a client lobbying Congress, NOAA and the Department of Commerce on weather data and forecast policy. Its chief executive Barry Myers was nominated to head NOAA in 2017; the nomination was withdrawn in 2019, after Myers had resigned from the company and sold his interest.

facts.claim: AccuWeather's origins trace to November 15, 1962, when Joel N. Myers, then a graduate student at Penn State, began forecasting winter weather for Columbia Gas, a Pennsylvania gas utility.
facts.quote: AccuWeather, Inc.'s origins can be traced back to November 15, 1962, when Dr. Joel N. Myers, then a graduate student at Penn State, began forecasting winter weather for Columbia Gas, a Pennsylvania gas utility.

facts.claim: A Senate lobbying disclosure filing lists AccuWeather as a client whose business is described as weather data and forecast services, with lobbying on science and technology issues directed at the Department of Commerce, NOAA, the House and the Senate.

facts.claim: CNN reported in 2017 that AccuWeather spent $40,000 in 2005 lobbying the House, Senate and Commerce Department through Blank Rome Government Relations on 'commercial weather industry issues', and that more recent disclosures showed it continuing to lobby Congress, NOAA and the Commerce Department on 'federal data policies'.

Senator Rick Santorum introduced S.786, the National Weather Services Duties Act of 2005, on April 14, 2005; it was referred to the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee and would have barred the National Weather Service from providing products that the private sector provides or could provide, except severe-weather warnings and forecasts to protect life and property.

facts.claim: AccuWeather paid $290,000 as part of a federal settlement of sexual harassment claims, a disclosure that drew criticism during Barry Myers's NOAA nomination; Myers was not personally accused of harassment.

openQuestions: Site claim that AccuWeather 'backed' Santorum's 2005 National Weather Services Duties Act was not confirmed by any source opened; the sources establish the bill's content and AccuWeather's 2005 lobbying on commercial weather industry issues, but not an explicit endorsement of S.786. The owner may wish to check contemporaneous reporting.
Site claim that the bill 'died' is consistent with the sources, which show no action beyond committee referral, but no source states its final disposition.
AccuWeather's OpenSecrets lobbying profile and annual totals were not retrieved.
Current leadership (a 2023 report said Steven R. Smith became CEO with Joel Myers as executive chairman) came only from an encyclopedia mirror and was not recorded.
